summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,200-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best videos pair a surprising claim about a simple gadget (clap switch, gyro robot, mic, heat sensor) with a short, punchy Hindi title. Longer, generic 'how does X work?' titles on everyday items (taps, doors, smoke alarms) get far fewer views and almost no saves or shares, and the English video and the older videos did poorly.
winningPattern: Hindi Shorts about a robot or a sound/heat/light sensor, with a 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it does the surprising thing' hook (e.g. 'Sensor sees nothing, only feels heat'; 'Clap switch listens to noise, not claps'). Titles are short (under 10 words) with one emoji, and the videos are posted to Instagram Reels first. Robots and clap-switch topics also did best on YouTube. A direct reversal ('X is the opposite of Y') drove the most saves and shares.
doMore: Open with a surprising reversal: 'X doesn't do Y, it does Z' in under 10 words
Make more robot and clap-switch / sound-sensor videos, since they won on both platforms
Post to Instagram Reels first and treat YouTube as a secondary test
Make follow-ups to winners (e.g. a part 2 of the gyro robot or the clap switch with whistling)
End with a question or a 'save this for your project' line to raise saves and shares
stopDoing: Generic titles like 'How does [everyday item] work?' for taps, doors and alarms
Posting several near-duplicate videos on the same topic (smoke alarm, IR sensor, clap switch variants) within days
Publishing English videos while the audience is responding to Hindi
nextTopics: Buzzer that works as a microphone
